prompt.context: Our client is a major US television network. They are trying to figure out how much to bid for the exclusive right to broadcast the 2018 Winter Olympics Games in the U.S. The Winter Olympics are a huge deal and will require a significant amount of capital to secure the rights, so our client has brought us in to help them figure out the right bid amount after considering all relevant factors.
prompt.question: How much should our client bid for the exclusive US broadcast rights to the 2018 Winter Olympics?

clarifying_info.q: Does the network earn subscription revenue from broadcasting the Olympics?
clarifying_info.a: No subscription revenue; the network can keep 100% of advertising revenue.
$400K per 30-second ad for prime time (Monday–Friday 7–11 PM, and all weekend) and $200K per ad for non-prime time.

clarifying_info.q: How many minutes of advertising are allowed per hour?
clarifying_info.a: Market research shows no more than 10 minutes of advertising per hour.

clarifying_info.q: Is there an opportunity cost to airing the Olympics?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, $1M per hour of airtime foregone from normal programming.

clarifying_info.q: What is the time value of money / discount rate?
clarifying_info.a: There is a 4-year lag for receipt of revenue; use a WACC of 10%.

exhibits.title: Winter Olympics Schedule
exhibits.shows: The broadcast schedule for the 2018 Winter Olympics, broken into three segments: Day 1 (Opening Ceremonies, Friday, 8–11 PM), Days 2–15 (Weekdays 9AM–12PM, 2–5PM, 7–11PM; Weekends 11AM–9PM), and Day 16 (Closing Ceremonies, Saturday, 8–11 PM).

framework: Define this as a cost-benefit / NPV analysis: bid should not exceed NPV of the project
Identify revenue streams: primarily advertising revenue (prime time vs. non-prime time ad slots)
Identify all costs: (1) production costs, (2) opportunity cost of displaced programming, (3) time value of money (discount rate)
Calculate total revenue from ad slots across the full schedule
Subtract production costs and opportunity costs to get undiscounted profit
Discount profit back at WACC over the 4-year lag to get NPV
Discuss qualitative / intangible factors that could adjust the bid above or below NPV
Arrive at a final bid recommendation with justification

questions.prompt: Calculate total advertising revenue from broadcasting the Winter Olympics.
questions.guidance: Candidate must break the schedule into segments (Opening/Closing Ceremonies, Weekday prime, Weekday non-prime, Weekend), apply the correct ad rate to each, and sum. Key formula per segment: days × hours/day × 10 min/hr × 2 slots/min × rate/slot.

math.setup: 10 min/hr of ads = 2 × 30-sec slots per minute × 10 min = 20 slots/hr. Prime time rate = $400K/slot; Non-prime time rate = $200K/slot. Schedule: Opening (Fri Day 1): 8–11 PM = 3 hrs prime. Days 2–14 Weekdays (10 weekdays): 7–11 PM = 4 hrs prime; 9AM–12PM + 2–5PM = 6 hrs non-prime. Days 3,7,8,9,14,15 Weekends (4 weekend days in days 2–15): 11AM–9PM = 10 hrs all prime. Closing (Sat Day 16): 8–11 PM = 3 hrs prime.
steps: Weekday prime (M-F, Days 2-15): 10 days × 4 hrs × 20 slots/hr × $400K = $320M
Weekday non-prime (M-F, Days 2-15): 10 days × 6 hrs × 20 slots/hr × $200K = $240M
Weekend prime (Days 2-15 weekends): 4 days × 10 hrs × 20 slots/hr × $400K = $320M

questions.prompt: Factoring in all costs, what is the NPV of the Olympics broadcast, and therefore the maximum bid?
questions.guidance: Candidate must subtract production costs and opportunity costs from revenue to get undiscounted profit, then discount at WACC over 4 years to get NPV. Opportunity cost: apply $1M/hr to total broadcast hours (Opening 3 hrs + 14 weekdays × 10 hrs + Closing 3 hrs = 146 hrs).

math.setup: Revenue = $928M. Production costs = $482M. Opportunity cost = $1M/hr × 146 total hours. Discount factor = (1.10)^4 ≈ 1.4641, rounded to 1.5.
steps: Opportunity cost hours: 2 ceremony days × 3 hrs + 14 broadcast days × 10 hrs = 6 + 140 = 146 hrs

brainstorming.prompt: Beyond the NPV, what intangible factors and qualitative considerations might influence how much the network should bid for the Olympics broadcast rights?

categories.name: Strategic / Brand Benefits
ideas: Prestige associated with hosting a major global sporting event
Signals network's position as a top-tier broadcast partner
Strengthens relationships with advertisers and sponsors

categories.name: Audience / Viewership
ideas: Access to new viewers who don't normally watch the network
Potential to convert casual Olympics viewers into regular network viewers
Demographic reach may differ from normal programming (e.g., sports fans, family viewers)

categories.name: Cross-Promotion
ideas: Air time to promote other network programming during high-viewership periods
Opportunity to launch new shows with a large captive audience
Drive awareness for upcoming season premieres

categories.name: Supplemental Revenue
ideas: Product tie-ins and sponsorship packages beyond standard ad slots
Digital/streaming rights that could layer on additional revenue

categories.name: Competitive / Game Theory
ideas: Other networks may bid aggressively; losing could mean losing market share
Winning could lock a competitor out for years
Bid strategy should consider rivals' likely valuations

categories.name: Risks
ideas: Event cancellation or disruption risk (weather, political, safety)
Lower-than-expected viewership in a non-US time zone
Cost overruns on production beyond the $482M estimate

recommendation: The network should bid approximately $200M, equal to the calculated NPV of the project.
This represents the maximum amount at which the investment breaks even on a risk-adjusted, discounted basis.

Intangible benefits (new viewer acquisition, cross-promotion, prestige) could justify a modest premium above $200M, but any upward adjustment must be accompanied by a concrete argument quantifying those benefits.
risks: Competitor bids may exceed $200M, requiring the client to choose between overpaying and losing the rights
Actual viewership or ad fill rates could fall short of assumptions, eroding the projected $928M in revenue
Production costs may exceed the $482M estimate
A 4-year delay in revenue receipt means capital is tied up for a long period with no interim return
next_steps: Conduct competitive intelligence on rival networks' likely bid ranges
Stress-test revenue assumptions (viewership scenarios, ad rate sensitivity)
Explore whether digital/streaming rights are included in the bid, which could add incremental value
Identify specific cross-promotion and tie-in revenue opportunities to quantify intangible upside
